title: IUD removal
what: A gynecologist takes the IUD out of the womb by pulling its strings. It is usually quick and done right in the exam room.
why: When the IUD has expired, when you plan a pregnancy, if you have side effects, or simply if you want it out.
duration: the procedure itself takes 1 to 5 minutes
tell_doctor: If you are planning a pregnancy
The date of your last period
If you had unprotected sex in the last 7 days
If you have pain, unusual discharge, or a fever

prepare.title: Protection
prepare.text: If you do not want to get pregnant and want a new IUD or another method, talk with your doctor ahead of time. You are usually advised to use protection for 7 days before removal.

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: The IUD is often removed during your period, but other days are possible too. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: Before your visit
prepare.text: Take a shower and bring a pad.

bring: Your referral, if you have one
Details about your IUD: when it was put in and what type, if you know
steps: You lie on the gynecology chair
The doctor puts in a speculum, a tool that gently opens the vagina
The doctor finds the IUD strings
With a special instrument, the doctor gently pulls the strings, and the IUD comes out
The doctor checks that the IUD is whole
feel: A short pulling pain, like period cramps
It usually passes in a few minutes
after: Light bloody spotting for 1 to 2 days is normal
You can get pregnant as soon as this cycle
If you are getting a new IUD, it is often put in at the same visit
If the strings cannot be seen, the doctor may order an ultrasound
red_flags: Heavy bleeding: more than one pad an hour
A fever above 38 degrees, or severe pain low in the belly

faq.a: It is usually unpleasant but quick: a few seconds of pulling pain.

faq.q: When can I get pregnant after IUD removal?
faq.a: Usually right away, in your next cycle. If you do not want a pregnancy, think about protection ahead of time.
